jenny.name: Jennifer Richards
jenny.title: English (2001) Chair
jenny.bio: Prior to joining Cambridge in 2023, Jennifer (FBA, FEA) was the Joseph Cowen Chair, Newcastle University, and the Director of the Humanities Research Institute.  Her areas of expertise include Renaissance English Literature, the history of reading, history of rhetoric (with a focus on delivery), and scholarly editing. Her most recent book, *Voices and Books in the English Renaissance: A New History of Reading*, was published by Oxford in 2019. It was out of this work on voice, rhetoric and reading that her interest in Charles Butler's study of the sound of bees began. As Chair of the English Association, and in collaboration with the School of Advanced Studies, London, she has launched an online series exploring collaboration: [‘Thinking Forwards’](https://englishassociation.ac.uk/thinking-forwards-collaboration/).

tiago.name: Tiago Sousa Garcia
tiago.title: Senior Research Software Engineer
tiago.bio: Tiago is a frontend web developer and digital humanist. Before his graduate and post-graduate education in literature, he worked as a software developer and studied computer engineering in Portugal. Between 2017 and 2021, he was the Research Associate for the *[ATNU](https://research.ncl.ac.uk/atnu/)* project, based at the School of English, where he also taught literary and digital humanities’ focused modules. In 2020-2021, he convened and ran the *Coding for Humanists* study group, and from 2022 he is one of the co-convenors of the *Code Community* at Newcastle University. Until 2022 he was a co-managing editor of the *[Journal of the Text Encoding Initiative](https://journals.openedition.org/jtei/)* and an editorial assistant for *[The Programming Historian](https://programminghistorian.org/en/)*
